text: Rosario Crocetta, born on 8 February 1951 in Gela, Sicily, is an Italian politician and openly gay man. He became the first openly gay mayor in Italy when he was elected Mayor of Gela in 2003, a position he held until 2009. His election followed a court ruling in 2003 that declared electoral fraud in the mayoral election, overturning the initial victory of right-wing candidate Giovanni Scaglione, who had won by a narrow margin of 197 votes. Telephone intercepts revealed that a local Mafia boss ordered a returning officer to prevent Crocetta, a center-left candidate, from winning, describing the effort as needing to "move heaven and earth in order to avoid the communist faggot to win." Crocetta, the son of a water-worker and a seamstress, began his political career in the 1980s with the Italian Communist Party, later joining the Communist Refoundation Party and the Party of Italian Communists. In 1998, he served as Councillor for Culture in Gela with the Federation of the Greens, focusing on cultural projects among Mediterranean countries, and from 2001 to 2002, he was Councillor for Public Education. In May 2002, he contested the mayoral election as a center-left candidate, and after the fraud was exposed, he was officially declared mayor. In 2007, he was re-elected with 64.4 percent of the vote. In 2008, he joined the Democratic Party and in the 2009 European elections, he was elected as a Member of the European Parliament for the Italian Islands constituency with 150,091 votes. In 2012, he ran for President of Sicily against Sebastiano "Nello" Musumeci of the PDL and eight other minor candidates on the platform of La Rivoluzione è Già Iniziata (The Revolution Has Already Started), winning 30.5 percent of the vote and becoming the first left-wing governor of Sicily since 1947. He served as President of Sicily from 2012 to 2017, making him the second openly gay head of a regional government in Italy after Nichi Vendola. From 2013 to 2017, he was also a member of the Committee of the Regions. On 19 July 2017, he announced his candidacy for the regional presidency with the list The Megaphone – Crocetta List, without Democratic Party support. After the party nominated Fabrizio Micari, Crocetta withdrew on 3 September 2017 and supported Micari with his list. Throughout his career, Crocetta has been a strong advocate against organized crime in Sicily and has faced multiple assassination plots. In 2003, a plot involving a Lithuanian killer targeting him during the patronal feast of the Immaculate Conception was thwarted by the Carabinieri. In 2008, a failed assassination attempt was revealed by the district attorney of Caltanissetta, leading to tighter security for Crocetta. In 2010, another assassination plot was stopped, resulting in the arrest of five individuals linked to the local Mafia. Crocetta speaks four languages—Italian, Arabic, English, and French—and has spoken and posted on social media in the Sicilian language. He worked for ENI in Gela after receiving his diploma and has an older brother, former PCI senator Salvatore Crocetta.
